Alex — thanks for the inventory. Attached is a concise planning artifact (redwood-remote-k8s-playbook-v1.pdf) and an NVMe sizing spreadsheet with a recommended baseline. High level recommendations below; more detail in the playbook: 

1) Minimal cluster footprint (production):
   - 3 control-plane nodes (t3-like CPU profile) spread across two racks for failure domain tolerance.
   - 6 worker GPU-capable nodes (one per 3U slot you mentioned) grouped into 2 node pools: 
       a) inference-pool (4 nodes, 2x A100-equivalent or local GPU choice) for low-latency serving,
       b) batch-train-pool (2 nodes, higher memory) for offline batch jobs and occasional canary testing.
   - All nodes labeled and tainted to support pinning (redwood/runtime=inference).

2) Storage zoning and PV strategy:
   - Local NVMe per worker for ephemeral model cache + KV caches (fast path). Use local PVs with node affinity.
   - Deploy a lightweight HA NFS cluster (3 replicas recommended) on separate utility nodes for durable artifacts and model artifacts that must survive node failure. This abides by your single-DC constraint.
   - Backups: scheduled rsync from NFS exports to a small on-site object store or offsite S3-compatible bucket (we'll support S3-compatible targets).
   - Default PV classes: local-nvme (fast), nfs-durable (durable), long-term-archive (object).

3) Networking & egress:
   - All outbound to Redwood control plane through your proxy with mTLS; we will supply a client cert template for the proxy team.
   - Use serviceCIDR that avoids overlap with your internal subnets; recommend a dedicated /20 for the cluster.
   - NodePort/SVC exposure only via a dedicated edge NAT/ingress appliance we will co-manage.

4) Security/compliance notes:
   - Audit logs: enable kube-audit and forward to your Splunk endpoint (we provide a fluentd manifest).
   - KMS/HSM: we can integrate with your KMS; provide key IDs and an account to validate.
   - Token rotation: implement short-lived service tokens + periodic pod identity refresh (we'll include a guide).

Action items for Ironbridge:
- Confirm if rack-level PDUs can support redundant power during maintenance windows (affects HA choices).
- Share NATed egress IPs and proxy cert provisioning window.
- Approve hardware SKU list in the attached NVMe sizing sheet so we can quote dedicated capacity.

We also attached a site checklist — looking for your go/no-go on the 2026-11-30 preflight window.

Best,

Alex / team — quick technical clarifications and notes from my side: 

- Local NVMe sizing: baseline assumes 2TB per inference node for model cache; if you plan to keep >3 model variants hot, bump to 4TB. See nvme-sizing-estimate.xlsx tab 'cache'.
- On NFS durability: prefer running the NFS server on 3 small VMs (utility nodes) with ZFS + replication if you cannot provision SAN. That gives us consistent exports and easier snapshotting.
- PV binding mode: use WaitForFirstConsumer for local-nvme volumes to ensure scheduling places pods where storage exists.
- GPU drivers: vendor-specific driver bundles will need to be preinstalled; provide us the BMC/console window to validate driver versions.

Also: for the non-redundant power, we'll include a fast node drain play in the runbook (graceful degraded mode) so single-rack failures are survivable for some SLA classes.

/dev
